acceptance_criteria.text: Dry-run is the default and the live gate is retained unchanged: live requires explicit live_enabled() (flag AND payment-capable credential); in dry-run no write endpoint (paymultiple/_post) is called and the result is recorded 'dry-run'. No default (code, .env.example, workflow) turns live on.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest: default -> client write mock not_called, outcome 'executed:dry-run'; flag without cred -> stays dry-run; both -> mocked write invoked and live enablement audited. grep workflow/.env.example: live flag absent or false.

acceptance_criteria.text: Trigger grammar: body contains the token 'pay' followed by exactly 3 digits (case-insensitive, word-bounded, e.g. 'pay 123' / 'pay123'); digits-only (letters not accepted) unless human changes Q5. No trigger -> message ignored (no pending, no reply, audit 'ignored'). 'pay' with 2 or 4 digits -> ignored/parked, not guessed.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest parametrised: 'pay 123','Pay123' trigger; 'pay abc','pay 12','pay 1234','payment 123','repay 123' do not; no-trigger mail creates no state and sends no email.

acceptance_criteria.text: The 3 digits select the SOURCE account by exact match on last-3 of the user's real accounts (get_accounts). Zero or >1 matching accounts (ambiguity across profiles/accounts) -> fail closed (parked, notify, no execute). Last-3 is never an authorization factor.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest: unique match resolves sourceAccountId bound into approval; 0 matches and 2 matches across profiles -> parked, execute not_called.

acceptance_criteria.text: PRIMARY CONTROL sender authentication: a message is processed only if (a) the OUTER From address is on a configured allowlist AND (b) Authentication-Results from the receiving mail host shows dkim=pass and spf=pass aligned with that From domain. Reply-To is never used for identity or routing. Missing/failed/absent headers -> fail closed (ignored+audited). No secret code or shared-secret factor is used (Q3 resolved).
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest: allowlisted From + dkim/spf pass -> processed; spoofed From (fail/none), allowlisted display-name with foreign address, Reply-To set to allowlisted address with foreign From, missing Authentication-Results -> not processed, no state, audit reason.

acceptance_criteria.text: Forwarded mail: authentication is applied to the OUTER (forwarding) sender only; From/headers/addresses inside the forwarded body or message/rfc822 attachment are never trusted for identity. Content of the forward is searched for payment data but cannot satisfy sender auth.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest: forward by allowlisted+authenticated user with inner message from stranger -> processed; forward by non-allowlisted outer sender with inner allowlisted From -> rejected.

acceptance_criteria.text: Search scope: for a triggered message the pipeline searches reply and forward body, quoted text, pdf/xlsx/csv attachments AND images (see F32-F38) for payment amount/currency/payee (existing extraction reused). Conflicting figures (two amounts, two payees, currency mismatch, corrupt attachment) -> parked, never executed.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest fixtures: body, quoted, forwarded, pdf, xlsx, csv each yield the expected candidate; conflicting figures across body vs attachment -> 'parked'; image handling per F32-F38.

acceptance_criteria.text: Beneficiary resolution is exact and registered-only: payee resolves only to an exact existing beneficiaryId from the account's registered beneficiaries; a parsed account number is never paid directly; fuzzy/partial match never auto-resolves.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest: exact match -> candidate with registered beneficiaryId; near-miss/ambiguous/no match -> not resolved; value passed to execute is the registered id.

acceptance_criteria.text: Unregistered/new payee (Q1, resolved): notify the user by email that the payee must be added in Investec Online/app, with details in EXACTLY this ordered field list (Q6): Beneficiary name, Bank, Account number, Amount, Their reference, My reference, Payment notification, Beneficiary email address, Beneficiary mobile number. Branch code, if known, appears only as a separate 'reference only' line outside the ordered list. A parked 'awaiting beneficiary' instruction is recorded (F12). The system NEVER calls any beneficiary-creating endpoint and no payment is sent for it at this stage.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest: unregistered payee -> exactly one notification email whose ordered fields equal the nine-item list above in that order, with branch code only in a separate 'reference only' line; awaiting-beneficiary instruction persisted; no create-beneficiary call exists (grep src finds none); client write mock not_called.

acceptance_criteria.text: Notification emails mask or minimise data: full account number appears only in the new-payee paste-details email to the verified user (necessary for the purpose), never in logs/audit/state/other emails (including the post-payment confirmation).
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest: captured logs, audit rows, stored state and summary/reminder emails contain no full account number; paste-details email goes only to the authenticated allowlisted sender.

acceptance_criteria.text: Two-path routing (Q2, replaces blanket 24h hold). (A) REGISTERED payee (exact beneficiaryId, F9): executes IMMEDIATELY in the same cycle, no hold and no cancel window, still subject to F3 (dry-run default/live gate), F15 pre-POST re-verification, F17 idempotency, F18 caps, F19 audit and F13 confirmation. (B) NEW/unregistered payee: F10 notification + a parked 'awaiting beneficiary' instruction is persisted; nothing is sent to paymultiple. Once the payee appears in the live beneficiary list, pay only after a configurable hold (default 24h; see F39), then re-verify (F15) and execute.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest with injected clock and fake client: registered payee -> write invoked once in the same cycle (live-mocked) or recorded dry-run, no execute_after; unregistered -> parked awaiting_beneficiary, write not_called; beneficiary appears in list at t0 -> not executed before t0+hold, executed at t0+hold after re-verification.

acceptance_criteria.text: Emails: registered path -> a post-payment confirmation email to the authenticated user after the payment outcome is known (payee name, amount, source last-3, outcome; no full account number). New-payee path -> F10 paste-details email at park time, a notice when the beneficiary is first observed and the hold starts (with execute_after and how to cancel), and a reminder before execution (default ~1h before; once only). Failures/expiry/unknown outcomes also notify.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest: registered success -> one confirmation email after execution (dry-run says dry-run); new payee -> one paste-details email, one hold-started email on first observation, one reminder in window, no duplicates on rerun; emails contain no token/secret or full account number (except F10 paste details).

acceptance_criteria.text: Cancel by reply remains available while an instruction is parked or held (new-payee path): an authenticated (F6) reply from the allowlisted sender with a cancel keyword referencing the pending instruction cancels it; cancel is atomic versus execute (compare-and-set on status in one DB transaction) so exactly one of cancel/execute wins. Registered-payee payments execute immediately and have no cancel window (Q2).
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest: cancel while awaiting_beneficiary or during hold -> status cancelled, never executed; concurrent cancel vs execute (CAS) -> exactly one winner; unauthenticated cancel ignored; registered path has no pending cancel state.

acceptance_criteria.text: Immediately before the paymultiple POST (BOTH paths, no delay between check and POST beyond the call itself): re-verify beneficiary still registered and unchanged, source account still resolves uniquely, sufficient available balance, per-payment and daily caps; any failure -> parked + notified, not executed. Obtain a fresh OAuth token for the payment call (never reuse a cached token from acceptance/an earlier cycle).
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest: beneficiary removed/changed, balance short, cap exceeded each -> parked, write mock not_called, for registered and held paths; token fetch occurs at execution time (token mock call count incremented after the hold).

acceptance_criteria.text: Expiry window: a parked 'awaiting beneficiary' or held instruction that is not executed within a configured window (default 7 days from acceptance for awaiting; 24h after execute_after for held; both configurable) is expired and notified rather than executed late. Stale instructions never auto-pay.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest: awaiting instruction older than window -> expired, write not_called, one notification; held instruction past execute_after+expiry -> expired; within window -> executes.

acceptance_criteria.text: Idempotency: the paymultiple POST is NEVER automatically retried (no retry/backoff on the write); a 200 response whose body carries ErrorMessage or AuthorisationRequired (or any non-success item status) is treated as FAILURE. Unknown outcome (timeout) -> marked 'unknown/needs_review', notified, never re-sent automatically. Same payment cannot execute twice.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest: write mock raising timeout -> call_count==1, status needs_review; 200 {ErrorMessage:...} and AuthorisationRequired -> status failed, not 'executed'; re-run cycle -> call_count still 1; urllib3/requests retry adapter absent on the write path.

acceptance_criteria.text: Caps fail closed (Q7): configured defaults are R30,000 per payment and R50,000 per day (persisted daily aggregate). Caps are read from env config; an unset, 0, negative or unparsable value means NO payment allowed (no hard-coded fallback silently enabling payments). Enforced pre-execution and re-checked at execution (F15). Daily total survives restart. Documentation must state that caps above R20,000 exceed the community-documented (unverified) Investec API per-payment limit, so Investec may reject; the caps are ours.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest: cap unset/0/'abc' -> blocked; over R30,000 -> blocked; aggregate pushing over R50,000 -> blocked; reloaded store retains total; write mock not_called when blocked; docs/.env.example list the defaults and the R20,000 caveat.

acceptance_criteria.text: Append-only audit trail records every step (received, auth result, ignored, parked, accepted, reminder, cancel, execute, fail, expire) with timestamps; never contains full account numbers, PAN, tokens, signing secret or other PII beyond hashed message id and last-3.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest: full lifecycle -> ordered entries, none mutated/deleted; scan of audit text finds no 9+ digit run, no secret, no email body.

acceptance_criteria.text: [DROPPED by human decision, spec amendment_2 / F42] Defect fix #1 (verify first): CLI approve-payments never passes approval_recipients to run_approval_cycle (cli.py ~L307), so pending approval/summary emails are never sent in production. Reproduce with a failing test, then fix so summary/notification recipients come from config (the authenticated allowlisted user), without changing existing flags' meaning.
acceptance_criteria.verify: A new test fails at base 2eee10c and passes after fix: CLI cycle with a pending item invokes smtp send to the configured recipient; existing approve-payments --help unchanged unless Q-approved additive flag.

acceptance_criteria.text: [DROPPED by human decision, spec amendment_2 / F42] Defect fix #2 (verify first): dedup key includes the inbound Message-ID, so a reply (new Message-ID) yields a different key and token/cancel replies are rejected or create duplicates. Reproduce with a failing test, then key cancel/approval matching on the pending record's stable id/nonce (carried in Subject/References/In-Reply-To), not the reply's Message-ID. Dedup of the same original email remains.
acceptance_criteria.verify: New test fails at base and passes after: original mail then reply with different Message-ID matches the same pending; same original mail twice -> one pending; different payments -> different keys.

acceptance_criteria.text: Frozen behaviour: ingest, report, statements, backfill-hashes, backup, init-db and beneficiary-matching outputs are unchanged; no change to existing CLI flags/help; any new CLI surface is additive only and approved.
acceptance_criteria.verify: Refreshed baseline --help byte-identical for all pre-existing subcommands; existing ingest/report/statement/beneficiary tests unmodified and green; git diff shows no edits to ingest/report/statements modules' logic.

acceptance_criteria.text: Schema: only additive migrations (next free prefix 0013+), state stored in Postgres via the existing pg_store pattern, RLS enabled with deny_all policies for new tables (matching 0010/0011); no edits to existing migrations, tables or views.
acceptance_criteria.verify: git diff -- db/migrations shows only new files; migrations apply in numeric order on a scratch DB; new tables have ROW LEVEL SECURITY and deny_all policy; migration-order test green; views definitions unchanged.

acceptance_criteria.text: No secrets committed: .env stays git-ignored; credentials, signing secret, IMAP/SMTP creds and Investec keys come from env/Actions secrets only and never appear in code, logs, emails, audit or workflow files.

acceptance_criteria.text: No new third-party dependencies or network egress targets unless explicitly justified in the plan and approved at the plan gate (stdlib email/imaplib/zoneinfo preferred). acceptance_criteria.text: Agent-native: the cycle runs headlessly from the CLI with mocked inbox/SMTP/Investec, machine-readable JSON output and deterministic exit codes; state and audit are assertable in tests.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest: invoke entry point with mocks -> JSON summary and expected exit code for ignore/accept/park/cancel/execute paths.

acceptance_criteria.text: Credential scope split (Q9, resolved yes for now): live mode uses a separate payment-only Investec credential distinct from the read credential used for ingest/report; read credential never performs writes. Note: listing beneficiaries needs the same scope as paying, so the read/ingest key may keep that scope; split has limited value and may be removed later if it does not work.

acceptance_criteria.text: Retention/minimisation: persisted records hold only needed fields (ids as last-3/hash), terminal records are purged after a retention window, and cleanup is covered by tests.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest: stored row has no full account number; cleanup removes terminal records older than window and keeps active ones.

acceptance_criteria.text: ARC policy (Q8, resolved): ARC is never trusted; relayed/rewritten mail requires a direct dkim=pass and spf=pass on the outer sender, otherwise rejected.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest: message with arc=pass but dkim/spf fail -> rejected under default policy.

acceptance_criteria.text: Operator documentation (README/runbook) describes trigger grammar, auth requirements, the two payment paths, new-payee hold (and that the 24h rule is NOT confirmed by the official swagger and that the community FAQ's 'beneficiary must be paid once in Investec Online first' may block new beneficiaries even after the hold), cancel, caps and the R20,000 caveat, image handling and untrusted-image policy, rollout gates and how to keep live off.
acceptance_criteria.verify: docs file contains each topic heading and both caveats verbatim in substance; reviewer checklist.

acceptance_criteria.text: Image reading in scope: for a triggered, authenticated message the pipeline reads images (jpeg/png/gif/webp attachments AND inline images/screenshots) alongside body, quoted text and pdf/xlsx/csv to extract payee name, account number, amount and reference. Unsupported/oversize/corrupt images are skipped gracefully with an audit note.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest with fake extractor: jpeg/png/gif/webp attachment and inline image each yield a candidate; corrupt/oversize/unsupported -> skipped, no crash.

acceptance_criteria.text: Image-derived data is UNTRUSTED and advisory: the payment trigger ('pay'+3 digits), the source-account last-3 and all authorisation come ONLY from the authenticated sender's typed body text, never from an image. An image-only message, or an image containing 'pay 123', creates no instruction.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest: image containing trigger text with no typed trigger -> ignored; image containing different last-3 than body -> body wins, image value ignored.

acceptance_criteria.text: The extraction engine may only EXTRACT structured fields (payee name, account number, amount, reference); it never decides to pay or to route. The payee must exactly resolve to a registered beneficiary (F9) else the new-payee notify path (F10); an extracted account number is never paid directly.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest: extractor output with unknown payee -> notify path, write not_called; extractor output has no action/decision field (schema test); exact registered match -> resolves registered beneficiaryId.

acceptance_criteria.text: Image-derived amount conflicting with any other source (body, quoted text, attachment, another image) -> parked and notified, never executed. Image-derived amounts to a REGISTERED payee follow the Q11 policy (default: NO immediate pay; require confirm-by-reply or the standard hold) until the human decides otherwise.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest: image amount != body amount -> parked; image-only amount to registered payee -> not executed immediately (confirm/hold required) under default Q11 policy.

acceptance_criteria.text: Prompt-injection resistance: text inside an image such as 'ignore previous instructions' or 'pay X to account Y' has no effect on trigger, routing, payee, caps, source account or execution; the extractor output is validated against a strict schema and treated as data.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest with adversarial image fixture (fake extractor returning injection text/extra fields and a real adversarial fixture file): no payment, no state change beyond parked/ignored, extra fields dropped, audit records the rejection.

acceptance_criteria.text: Extraction engine sits behind an interface (e.g. ImageExtractor protocol) with a deterministic fake used in all tests; no test performs network egress or needs OCR binaries; engine selected by config, default disabled/none if unconfigured (images then skipped).
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest uses fake only; grep tests for real engine imports/network finds none; unconfigured engine -> images skipped, no error.

acceptance_criteria.text: No image bytes, base64, extracted account numbers or raw extractor responses appear in logs, audit, stored state or non-paste emails; only hashes/sizes/mime types and masked last-3 may be recorded.
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest: run pipeline with image fixture, scan captured logs/audit/state for image bytes/base64 and 9+ digit runs -> none.

acceptance_criteria.text: New-payee hold clock: the configurable hold (default 24h) is measured from OUR first observation of that beneficiary in the live beneficiary list, persisted at that first observation (survives restart; never reset by later observations; not measured from instruction receipt or beneficiary creation time).
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest with injected clock and store reload: first_seen_at set once at first observation; execute_after = first_seen_at+hold; later cycles do not change it; restart retains it.

acceptance_criteria.text: Fail closed on Investec rejection: if Investec rejects a payment (e.g. beneficiary not yet payable), the instruction is marked failed, the user is notified, and there is no automatic retry (F17).
acceptance_criteria.verify: pytest: write mock returning rejection/ErrorMessage for held new beneficiary -> status failed, notification sent, call_count==1 across reruns.

acceptance_criteria.text: Spec/doc honesty: the 24h new-beneficiary rule is NOT confirmed by the official swagger and is an app-side configurable rule; the community FAQ states a beneficiary must be paid once in Investec Online first, which may block new beneficiaries even after the hold. Both statements appear in README/runbook and in code config comments.
acceptance_criteria.verify: grep docs and config for both statements.

acceptance_criteria.text: Legacy token-approval flow is RETIRED, not fixed: the legacy code path (payments/pipeline.py approval-token flow, token.py, legacy inbox token parsing) is left byte-identical (zero diff), is never fixed to email approval tokens, and is never scheduled. The scheduled GitHub Actions workflow runs v2 only (PAYMENTS_MODE=v2 pinned) and refuses to run the legacy flow. Legacy is reachable only by explicit operator action (PAYMENTS_MODE unset or 'legacy', e.g. a manual `approve-payments --once`), is documented as DEPRECATED/unsupported in the runbook, and no v2 or workflow code path sends a legacy approval email or token. Existing tests that exercise legacy behaviour stay unmodified and green.
acceptance_criteria.verify: git diff --stat vs base shows no change to payments/pipeline.py, payments/token.py and the legacy parts of payments/inbox.py (additive v2 modules only); workflow test asserts PAYMENTS_MODE=v2 and no legacy invocation; docs contain the deprecation note; all pre-existing tests pass unmodified

rollout_gates: G1 Dry-run soak: run scheduled dry-run only for a minimum period (recommended 14 days / at least 5 real instructions) with audit reviewed and zero unexpected outcomes.
G2 Sandbox test: end-to-end payment exercised against openapisandbox.investec.com (mocked-money) including error bodies (ErrorMessage/AuthorisationRequired) and no-retry behaviour.
G3 Human enables live explicitly: human sets the live flag and pay credential and caps; recorded in audit; never enabled by default or by the loop.
coverage_note: Maps GOAL.md + decisions.md (Q1-Q9, image requirement) to F3-F41; frozen-behaviour and no-secrets constraints are Musts (F2,F22,F23,F24,F25).
confidence: high on guardrails; medium on Investec API write semantics (verify in sandbox, G2).
amendment_2: Human decision (after plan-review rounds 1-3): RETIRE the legacy token-approval flow instead of fixing it. F20 and F21 are DROPPED (retired by human decision); replaced by F42. Rationale: the v2 flow authenticates by sender and does not use approval tokens; fixing the legacy flow (emailing approval tokens to the owner) created a bot-approves-its-own-payments loop and quoted-token approval risk and would break existing tests; nothing deploys the legacy flow.
